name: Axiscades Technologies Ltd
title: Axiscades Technologies Ltd - 532395 - Updated Transcript Of The Earnings Webinar - Q4 & FY26

read.thesis: Q4 FY26 revenue fell short: a ₹142 cr deferment and ₹40 cr+ EBITDA hit pushed reported PAT to ₹72 cr, and FY27 leans on deferred orders, a divestment and an unfunded ₹2,100–2,250 cr capex-plus-M&A plan.

summary.headline: FY26 revenue rose 12.4% to ₹1,159 crore and EBITDA 24.6% to ₹178 crore, but reported PAT fell 4.3% to ₹72 crore on a ₹142 crore Q4 revenue deferment.
summary.overview: Management framed FY26 as a strong operating year with a weak Q4: operating metrics (revenue, EBITDA, EBIT, pre-exceptional PBT) grew, while reported PAT was hit by a ₹142 crore Q4 revenue deferment (~₹40 crore EBITDA impact), restructuring exceptional items (~₹11.17 crore), and a higher FY26 tax charge. Q4 alone had revenue of ₹273 crore, EBITDA of ₹34 crore and PAT of ₹0.4 crore. The company signed the divestment of its heavy engineering, energy and automotive services practice to Akkodis (USD 30.63 million) and is pursuing Phase 2 disinvestment, two ESAI and two aerospace acquisitions, and a Power 930 target of ₹9,000 crore revenue by FY30. Receivables were ₹411 crore at year-end (DSO 130 days), with ₹154.5 crore collected since March and DSO cited at 81 days.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹388 crore, up 21% YoY, with EBITDA margin of 17.3%. Management says it will move toward manufacturing via an acquisition expected to start high-value manufacturing in Q3 FY27.

segments.name: Defense
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹379 crore, up 25% YoY, with EBITDA margin of 22.9%. Includes land systems contracted with MoD, with ~₹100 crore WIP awaiting MoD pre-dispatch inspection.

segments.name: ESAI (electronics, semiconductor, AI)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue ₹136 crore, up 9% YoY, with EBITDA margin of 26.1%. Being moved into new US-led subsidiary Xida Inc.; management cites roughly $15 million annual revenue.

segments.name: Core domains combined (aerospace, defense, ESAI)
segments.commentary: Approximately ₹904 crore of FY26 revenue, about 78% of consolidated revenue, per management. Divested engineering services (heavy engineering, energy, automotive) sits outside this group.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue trending to ₹1,377 crore, a 52% increase on retained FY26 base of ₹903 crore; visibility split into ₹927 crore order under execution (including the ₹142 crore deferred), ₹284-285 crore assured forecast, and ₹165 crore acquisition-linked.
₹142 crore Q4 deferred revenue expected to be recognised across Q1 and Q2 FY27, subject to delivery, inspection and customer acceptance.
Akkodis divestment expected to close in Q2 FY27 (around July-August 2026), with an extraordinary gain of ~₹175 crore (about ₹41 per share EPS).
Core-vertical EBITDA margin targeted to improve by 150-200 bps YoY; management said margin expansion will saturate around 25-27%.
Power 930 target of ₹9,000 crore revenue by FY30; management says ₹960 crore PAT could be reached on ~₹7,200 crore revenue, possibly before FY30.
Approximately ₹120-140 crore cash expected to be released in H1 FY27 as deferred programmes deliver and collect.
ESOP: about 3.8 million options to be awarded by Q1-Q2 FY27, funded by the transaction proceeds; headcount expected to fall from ~2,800 to ~1,200 after restructuring.
capex_capacity: Three facilities (DAC, DAL, MAC) total ~₹1,550-1,600 crore including spend to date; DAC ~₹1,200 crore, MAC ~₹300 crore, DAL ~₹150 crore spent so far. ₹96 crore invested in DAL, DAC and MAC in FY26 from internal accruals.
Devanahalli campuses and MAC Hyderabad to become operational through FY27; DAL targeted ready by year-end, with DAC and MAC to follow.
Hyderabad land (~8.2 acres, ~₹40 crore) capitalised in non-current assets; Aeroland facility (~1,65,000 sq ft) taken on new lease.
Acquisitions budgeted at ~₹600 crore (two aerospace ~₹400-450 crore, two ESAI ~₹50 crore and ~₹150 crore); total capex plus acquisitions ₹2,100-2,250 crore.
Phase 1 divestment ₹293 crore pre-tax; management expects Phase 2 disinvestment to be a larger event, scheduled for H1 FY27, to fund the remainder.
demand_pricing: Q4 deferments: ₹45 crore defense land-systems programme (supplier constraint, since resolved); ₹84 crore strategic electronics programme (monopolistic hardware supplier diverted output to war-related programmes; inputs now secured); ₹12.6 crore aerospace & defence contract deferred during Akkodis transition.
Defense pipeline focused on large programmes (swarm drones, CLRTS, HAL-linked); company says it is shortlisted among 3-5 bidders for most; 21 DRDO design wins referenced.
ESAI: Qualcomm order of $3.5 million in recent months with a pipeline of $0.5-1 million per month; customers include TI, Qualcomm, a hyperscaler, a large consumer-tech company, AXON and Aptiv.

Management said government offset policy has been slowed or stopped, and new contracts since 2025 are oriented to Atmanirbhar; OEM JVs/contracts expected to complete around Q3 FY27, subject to Government of India approval.

qa_highlights.question: How will the ₹9,000 crore FY30 revenue target (about 10x FY26) be achieved, and has it been scaled down?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is not being scaled down. The plan is to convert design work into design-cum-manufacturing, with order books expected to build in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Will core-segment margins reach 20% and beyond, and what is the post-FY27 order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Core verticals already average above 20% EBITDA; management targets 150-200 bps YoY improvement. Pipeline will be quantified after Q1 FY27 results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the structure of the Akkodis deal and the earn-out?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a slump sale; guaranteed consideration of $23.4 million, with 75% paid at closing and 25% after one year. A further $7.4 million earn-out depends on FY27 EBITDA targets. Company will hand-hold the buyer for one year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the ₹9,000 crore revenue and ~₹960 crore PAT target imply the PAT goal is underscored?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ₹960 crore PAT needs only ~₹7,200 crore revenue at a 25%+ PAT margin, so the PAT goal could be reached earlier than FY30.

qa_highlights.question: How is FY26 cash flow funded given ₹1,100-1,200 crore capex plus acquisitions and rising short-term debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 2 disinvestment is expected to fund the programme without equity dilution or new long-term debt; only working-capital and bridge debt is planned.

qa_highlights.question: What is the end product, TAM and timing for space and Xida/ESAI?
qa_highlights.answer: Xida will consolidate ESAI (about $15 million revenue); two acquisitions are being evaluated. Space focuses on space bus, payload and SAR; management will give details around late June or early July with no revenue timing given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin trajectory, and could PAT exceed guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin gains will saturate around 25-27%, with aerospace manufacturing expected to lift the average toward ~23%. Revenue will be the main lever, with the 'architect to builder' shift cited.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex, capital allocation and acquisition plans after the ₹293 crore divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Phase 1 proceeds are called a 'modest beginning'. Phase 2 and internal accruals are expected to cover ~80% of the ₹2,100-2,250 crore plan; the rest is expected from internal accruals, partnerships or JVs.

risks_watch: Execution of the ₹142 crore Q4 deferred revenue in Q1-Q2 FY27 (MoD pre-dispatch inspection of ~₹100 crore land systems WIP, strategic electronics input supply) and whether ₹120-140 crore cash is released in H1 FY27.

Phase 2 disinvestment timing: management has moved it to H1 FY27 and said it has 'delayed a bit'; it is needed to fund the ₹2,100-2,250 crore capex plus acquisition plan without dilution or new long-term debt.
Akkodis closing in Q2 FY27 and the ~₹175 crore extraordinary gain; ~$7.4 million earn-out tied to FY27 EBITDA; 25% deferred consideration after one year.
Credibility of FY30 ₹9,000 crore revenue target versus FY26 base of ~₹900 crore retained; management has not quantified the pipeline until Q1 FY27 results.
Receivables and DSO (411 crore, 130 days at year-end, 81 days now) and working capital; gross borrowings up to ₹276 crore.

Acquisition closings (two aerospace ~₹400-450 crore, two ESAI ~₹50 crore and ~₹150 crore) and OEM JVs expected around Q3 FY27 subject to Government of India approval; space and Xida revenue timing not given.
key_quotes: We did not have a bad year, we had a building year.
The reported PAT did not reflect that operating progress.
So, automatically, we are not scaling it down, we are sticking to 9000.
And there is no… this thing in my mind, but as we said, I will be able to give much more details.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on strategy, FY27 and Power 930, but defensive on the Q4 miss, attributing it to timing and supply-chain deferrals. Evasive or non-committal on specifics: pipeline size, space and ESAI revenue timing, Phase 2 disinvestment date, and the 20%+ margin path were deferred to Q1 FY27 results or a site visit.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to ₹1,377 crore (+52% on ₹903 crore retained base), backed by ₹927 crore order under execution (incl. ₹142 crore deferred), ₹284-285 crore assured forecast and ₹165 crore acquisition-linked; capacity (DAC, MAC, DAL) is under construction for FY27 with no per-facility output numbers, and the ₹142 crore deferral and ₹600 crore M&A add execution risk.
